body:
ACCIDENTAL-LEAK LEAD: Formal invariant: every byte observable from Audience HTTP/WSS/DOM/storage/cache/telemetry must be a function ONLY of `PublishedAudienceCard`, never Candidate/Transcript/RAG/Console state. Enforce structurally: Audience service account can read only a separate `published_cards` store/topic; it has no credentials/network path to private DB/event bus. Publish writes an immutable schema (`additionalProperties:false`) of plain-text title/body, approved asset hash, public canonical citations/attribution, alt text, expiry. It rejects HTML/Markdown, unknown fields, internal URI/doc IDs, prompts/queries/transcript/speaker/team/ACL/provider/debug fields. Console sends only `candidate_id`; server builds DTO—client/model never submits audience JSON.

`SUPPORTED` is necessary, not sufficient: `publishable = evidence_supported AND source_current AND audience_classification=PUBLIC AND rights=publishable AND privacy_DLP=pass AND presenter_approval`. Default manual WYSIWYG audience preview. Internal-RAG-derived cards never auto-publish; for 5s auto mode, restrict to approved public corpus + no detected person/secret + deterministic template. DLP checks secrets, credentials, emails/phones/IDs, internal domains/IPs, classification labels and source ACL metadata; uncertainty fails private. Audience errors are generic, with correlation ID only—never stack/provider response/search query.

Display-mode fail-safe: before private snapshot delivery, show Public Test Pattern on Audience and Privacy Curtain on Console; presenter confirms physical placement, producing `topology_fingerprint + display_instance + verified_at`. Extended mode subscribes to `screenschange/currentscreenchange`; any screen removal/change or uncertainty immediately curtains Console and stops private events until re-confirmed. Window Management API is experimental/limited and cannot detect every OS mirroring/capture case, so this is risk reduction, not a guarantee. In mirrored mode, presentation PC gets ONLY AudienceDisplaySession and never logs into Console; private Console runs on paired personal device. Recommend this mode whenever confidentiality matters.

Operational leakage controls: persistent PUBLIC/PRIVATE color+watermark chrome; emergency privacy-curtain control; raw transcript/source collapsed and press-to-reveal; no team-message link previews; browser notifications/session replay/APM screenshots disabled; Windows Do Not Disturb preflight; share only Audience window, never desktop. Console: no-store, no sensitive SW/Cache API/IndexedDB/localStorage, Clear-Site-Data on end/logout, privacy curtain on pagehide; Audience origin disables microphone/camera/display-capture/notifications and loads only self-hosted scripts/assets. No app can prevent OS screenshots, HDMI mirroring, OBS or shoulder surfing—remote private device is the hard mitigation.

Leak tests: packet/DOM/storage inspection proves Audience never sees private fields; fuzz unknown/PII/internal fields rejects publication; reconnect snapshot is role-filtered; error injection remains generic; topology event curtains before next private render; mirror workflow has no Console cookie; expired card disappears; service worker offline serves no private snapshot; logs/APM contain IDs only.

Sources: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ScreenDetails ; https://www.w3.org/TR/window-management/ ; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Permissions-Policy/display-capture ; https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Logging_Cheat_Sheet.html ; https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Error_Handling_Cheat_Sheet.html ; https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/HTML5_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html
